reader.requirement: At --std 85 the names a contained program B can reach are its own names plus the global names (data, condition, file, record, report, and index-names via X.1.3.8.3) of every program containing it, never a non-global name of a container nor any name of a sibling; qualification and uniqueness are applied over that whole set, so a qualified reference reaches a container's global item even past B's own declaration of the qualifier's spelling.

edition-consulted.switches: Year < 2002: condition-names, data-names and record-names are one disjoint set, so a level-88 and a data item of one tier reached by the same reference are counted together (COBOL-85 only)
counts the rival condition-names beside data items at 85; returns 0 at 2002+
counts the rival data items beside a level-88 at 85; returns 0 at 2002+
nothing: the name-set resolver is edition-free; the tier rules are the same code at 85 and 2023

reader.edition-search: grep for Edition./Year/DialectLevel/1985 in SymbolTable.NameSet.cs, SymbolTable.Declarations.cs, InheritStep.cs, SymbolTable.Files/Configuration/Constants/IndexNames.cs, ReportScope.cs: only comments name 1985; the edition reaches these rules only through the 85 disjoint-set counting
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes, narrowly: at 85 a level-88 and a data item are one disjoint set, so they are counted together inside a tier; the set of names itself is built the same way at 85 and 2023
reader.witnesses-cover: part: witnesses cover hidden global files/reports qualifying counters and the nearest declaring element; not exercised there: non-global container names and sibling globals left out of the set, three-level containment with qualification past an intermediate global, global index and ODO tables

probes.expected: refused: A's non-global Y is not in B's set
refused: a sibling's global X is not in the set
